area: bitchat's DM crypto: ECDH, HKDF, and the "v2:" payload framing
warning: This is NOT the published NIP-44 v2. The HKDF salt is empty and the info is "nip44-v2" - the published spec uses them the other way round. Swapping them yields a key that silently decrypts nothing bitchat ever sent.

ecdh.name: compressed_point_shared_secret
ecdh.derivation: swift-secp256k1 0.21.1 Sources/ZKP/ECDH.swift replaces libsecp256k1's default ECDH hash function with hashClosure(), which writes ((y & 1) | 0x02) followed by x - the 33-byte COMPRESSED POINT. Not SHA-256 of the point, and not the 32-byte x coordinate. Point multiplication done with a pure-python secp256k1 validated against the generator multiples G and 2G and against all 8 signing vectors in BIP-340's CSV. Both keys were chosen to have even Y (scanning sha256(label + i)) so that the x-only wire form reconstructs to the real point and the two sides agree on the first attempt; the odd-Y case is parity_retry below.
ecdh.note: 33 bytes, and identical in both directions. The two wrong_ fields are the two plausible mistakes: dropping the prefix byte, or leaving libsecp256k1's default SHA-256 hash function in place. Both must differ from shared_secret_hex.

parity_retry.name: odd_y_sender_pubkey
parity_retry.source: NostrProtocol.decrypt (attemptDecrypt with 0x02 prefix, then 0x03 on failure)
parity_retry.derivation: A sender secret whose public point has odd Y, found by scanning sha256("chatter-mesh-nostr odd-y " + i) for the first i whose compressed prefix is 0x03; the recipient is the even-Y bob from the ecdh vector. shared_secret_odd_y is what the SENDER computes (it holds the recipient's real point); shared_secret_even_y_guess is what the RECIPIENT computes on its first attempt, reconstructing the sender's x-only key as even-Y - which is the negated point, so the x coordinate is identical and only the parity byte differs. Both computed with the validated pure-python secp256k1.
parity_retry.note: The event's pubkey field is x-only, so parity is lost on the wire. A recipient that only ever tries the even-Y reconstruction cannot decrypt from this sender at all - roughly half of all senders. That is what the 0x03 retry exists for.

hkdf.name: conversation_key_from_shared_secret
hkdf.derivation: HKDF-SHA256(ikm = the 33-byte compressed ECDH point, salt = empty, info = "nip44-v2", L = 32). CryptoKit's HKDF.deriveKey with an empty salt feeds HMAC a 32-byte all-zero key, which is what RFC 5869 specifies for an absent salt; the HKDF here was validated against RFC 5869 test cases 1 and 3, the latter covering exactly that empty-salt path.
hkdf.note: The last three are traps, each the output of one plausible wrong implementation (published-NIP-44 orientation, x-only ikm, hashed ikm). None may equal conversation_key_hex.

payload.name: v2_framing_roundtrip
payload.derivation: payload = "v2:" + base64url_nopad(nonce24 || ciphertext || tag16), with ciphertext and tag from the validated XChaCha20-Poly1305 above. base64url per Base64URLCoding.encode: standard base64 with + -> -, / -> _, and '=' stripped.
payload.note: Both directions: sealing plaintext_utf8 under this key and nonce must produce this payload, and opening this payload as the recipient must produce plaintext_utf8. The conversation key is HKDF over ECDH(sender, recipient), so the keypairs are given too.

payload.name: v2_payload_from_odd_y_sender
payload.derivation: Same construction as v2_framing_roundtrip, but the conversation key comes from the odd-Y sender in parity_retry above.
payload.note: This one only opens if the even-Y attempt is retried with 0x03. An implementation missing the retry fails here and nowhere else, then fails silently against half of all real senders.

malformed_payloads.name: wrong_version_prefix
malformed_payloads.why: Only v2 exists; anything else is rejected rather than guessed at.

malformed_payloads.name: exactly_nonce_plus_tag
malformed_payloads.why: decrypt requires count > 24 + 16 strictly, so a zero-length ciphertext is rejected.

malformed_payloads.name: shorter_than_nonce
malformed_payloads.why: Too short to even contain the nonce.

malformed_payloads.name: tampered_tag
malformed_payloads.why: Well-formed framing, forged tag: must fail authentication, not return garbage.

malformed_payloads.name: tampered_ciphertext
malformed_payloads.why: Flipped ciphertext byte must fail the Poly1305 check.
